Hi Neha,

Thanks for the RFP materials. Our security and procurement teams reviewed Appendix A (audit logging and retention). A few clarifications before we proceed to scoring:

1) Export formats: Appendix A asks for delivery formats. Can Redwood confirm supported export formats (e.g., JSONL, Parquet, CSV) and whether exports preserve nested event metadata (trace ids, session ids, KV pairs)?

2) Integrity & tamper-evidence: We need to understand how Redwood demonstrates the authenticity of exported logs (checksums, signed manifests, time-stamped hashes, chain-of-custody).

3) Retention categories: Can you map your retention windows by event category (admin audit, system events, user request logs, crytpo keys access logs)? We have a minimum retention requirement of 7 years for certain compliance events.

4) Legal hold & emergency export: If a legal hold is issued, what is the process and SLA to preserve and export affected records?

5) Delivery mechanics: Our ops team needs expected delivery modes (S3 presigned upload, direct SFTP, physical drive) and a rough time-to-delivery for a 1TB audit bundle.

Please loop in anyone on your side who owns exports so we can resolve quickly. We have a tentative procurement review on Jan 20.

Appreciate a short reply with proposed next steps.

Thanks,

Hi Karen —

Thanks for the clear list. I own the compliance/RFP response for this deal; looping Ben (platform ops) and Marissa (legal) to cover technical and contractual items. High-level answers below and I'll attach a short appendix with field-level mappings. See attached: appendix-A-log-specs.pdf.

Quick answers:
- Formats: We support JSONL (primary), Parquet (columnar for analytics), and compressed CSV exports for simple delivery. Exports preserve nested metadata (trace_id, session_id, request_id, kv pairs) in JSONL or Parquet; CSV is flattened which can lose nested structures.
- Integrity: Exports include a signed manifest containing SHA256 checksums per file, a manifest-level SHA256, and an RFC-3339 timestamp. For added assurance we can provide a notarized time-stamp via our audit service on request.
- Retention by category: Default retention (hosted) is 365 days for request logs, 3 years for elevated admin audit events, and 7 years for compliance-designated events; these can be configured under Dedicated/Private plans.
- Legal hold: We have a documented legal-hold workflow; upon notice, relevant objects are immutably tagged and excluded from retention expiries within 24 hours, and export work starts within agreed SLA.
- Delivery: Preferred is S3 presigned multipart upload (fastest), SFTP is supported for smaller bundles, and physical shipment is available for very large datasets under NDA. Typical baseline for a 1TB audit bundle to S3 presigned: 48-96 hours from export start depending on queue and region.

Next steps: Ben will follow up with technical delivery specifics and Marissa will propose contract language for legal hold and retention SLAs. If you can send the sample manifest you expect, we will map fields and confirm.

Best,

Karen / Neha —

Adding technical detail on delivery and integrity:

- File layout: Exports are produced as compressed file sets (gzip by default) containing either JSONL files (event-per-line) or Parquet row groups. Each export run is stamped with an export_id and sequence number (export_id: acme-20260113-0001).
- Nested metadata: In JSONL we keep full nested objects. Parquet exports include logical types so analytics engines (e.g. Athena/BigQuery via external table) can map nested fields.
- Checksums & signing: We compute SHA256 for each file and generate a signed manifest. The manifest is PGP-signed using Redwood's export signing key; we can instead provide HSM-backed time-stamp signatures for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Chain-of-custody: Manifest includes export_id, exporter service agent id, start/end timestamps, object list with sizes and checksums, and an export signer key fingerprint. We keep a retention-infinite audit trail of export operations in our internal export ledger (immutable append-only entries) for 10 years and can provide ledger slices on request.
- Encryption: Exports are encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.3) and at-rest in your target S3 if using server-side encryption; we also support client-side encryption where you provide the envelope key.
- Redaction/pseudonymization: Field-level redaction can be done during export: either (a) deterministic tokenization (pseudonymization) for PII fields, or (b) redaction to remove values. We provide a mapping file for tokenization to a customer-owned KMS under Private deployments.
- Estimated throughput & SLA: For presigned S3 multipart uploads we provision parallel workers; typical throughput is 400-600 MB/s aggregate per dedicated export job under our Dedicated plans. For hosted exports, expect lower and queue-based scheduling.

If you can drop a sample manifest and a list of the 1TB dataset's composition (percentage of JSON vs binary attachments), we'll produce a firm timeline and presigned batch plan.

Ben Carter
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

2) Retention mapping: Your earlier note says "default retention (hosted) is 365 days" — we need contractual confirmation that compliance-designated events are retained for 7 years and cannot be auto-deleted on hosted plans without a written exception. Is that acceptable or do we need Dedicated/Private?

3) Legal hold SLA: For legal hold we require immutability within 24 hours and an export start within 48 hours of the hold notice for datasets up to 2TB. Please confirm your ability to meet those SLAs and the escalation path (names/contacts).

4) Proof-of-delivery: We require: (a) signed manifest (PGP or HSM signature), (b) per-file checksums, (c) CMS-style chain-of-custody statement, and (d) a final export acceptance form signed by our security or authorized delegate.
